version.changelog:
Chonkie DeepResearch initial release:

- Run deep research queries and receive comprehensive reports with citations.
- Ideal for market analysis, competitive intelligence, technical deep dives, and any research-heavy tasks.
- Requires the Chonkie CLI tool (`chdr`) and an API key for authentication.
- Supports report management: list, view, open, and delete research via CLI.
- Reports can be very large; tools and workflow provided for efficient reading and answering follow-up questions.

llm.summary: The skill's purpose and required binary (chdr) match a research tool, but the runtime instructions ask the agent to run remote installers (curl | sh) and reference an environment variable (CHONKIE_API_KEY) that is not declared — those inconsistencies and the installer pattern raise concern.

dimensions.detail: Name/description match the observed requirements: the skill is an instruction-only wrapper around the chdr CLI for deep research. Requiring a chdr binary is coherent with the stated purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs the agent to run chdr commands, write outputs to /tmp, grep and read parts of generated .md files — all reasonable for report handling. HOWEVER the instructions explicitly recommend installing Rust by downloading and executing a remote installer (`curl ... | sh`) and to `cargo install chdr` if chdr is missing. That tells the agent to fetch and run remote code, and also references the CHONKIE_API_KEY env var (for authentication) even though it is not declared in the skill manifest.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no formal install spec (instruction-only), which is low-risk in itself, but the runtime install instructions recommend running `curl --proto ... https://sh.rustup.rs | sh` and `cargo install chdr`. The `curl | sh` pattern downloads and executes remote code (high-risk) unless done manually and reviewed. The skill does not provide a vetted release URL for a chdr binary or an audited package source.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The manifest declares no required env vars, but the instructions say you can set CHONKIE_API_KEY and point to the service's API key page — that env var is reasonable for the service but should be declared in requires.env. No other unrelated credentials are requested.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not always: true, does not request system-wide config paths, and is instruction-only. It does not ask to modify other skills or system configs. The primary risk is runtime execution of installer commands, not persistent privileges.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to be a thin wrapper around the chdr CLI and generally matches its description, but there are two things to watch: (1) SKILL.md tells the agent to install Rust by piping a remote installer to the shell (curl | sh). Prefer installing Rust and chdr yourself manually or using a vetted package rather than letting an agent execute that command. (2) The instructions reference CHONKIE_API_KEY but the manifest doesn't declare it — confirm that the skill will only ever use an API key for the chonkie service and that you understand its scope. If you plan to install/use this skill, manually install and verify the chdr binary from a trusted source (or declare a vetted install mechanism), only provide an API key with minimum required permissions, and avoid granting the agent autonomous permission to run the installer or arbitrary shell commands.
